short: Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound

title.title: Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
title.subtitle: Claim: cylinders can cover a regular tetrahedron with total cross-section below half its smallest shadow

plain: Wrap a pyramid in straight tubes: must the tubes' total cross-section be at least half its smallest shadow?

object.heading: Cylinders covering a tetrahedron: cross-section over smallest shadow
object.axisLabel: total base area of the cylinders, normalized

beats.text: Bang's two cylinders cover it at exactly half its smallest shadow
16,000,000 cylinders in nearby directions dip about $5 \times 10^{-10}$ below it

steps: Start from the two cylinders that meet the bound exactly
Split them into many cylinders, tilted in nearby directions
Triangular cross-sections save a second-order sliver of area

achievement.note: Refutes the $1/2$ bound; the true constant lies between $1/3$ and just under $1/2$

verify.detail: In Lean: the expansion and the strict counterexample. Not: the extension to every tetrahedron
verify.ourCheck: From the papers and their Lean docs; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Two cylinders cover it at exactly half its smallest shadow. Zoom in below one half.
Tilt many cylinders slightly apart; triangular sections save a sliver.
Claimed: below one half, by a sliver.

sources.quote: whose total base area, normalized by sqrt2, is 1/2 - (13/6000) eps^2 + O(eps^4) for 0<eps<=1/2000, hence strictly below half the minimum projection area
who proved the directionwise sum is >= 1/3 in R^3

sources.ref: article, Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
sources.quote: At the largest allowed $\epsilon = 1/2000$ that is about $5 \times 10^{-10}$, bought with $2\lceil 2/\epsilon^2\rceil$ = 16,000,000 cylinders.

sources.ref: article, Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
sources.quote: That refutes the $1/2$ constant and leaves the truth somewhere between Bezdek and Litvak's $1/3$ and just under $1/2$.
Per lean/docs/100.md the affine extension to every nondegenerate tetrahedron is outside the selected statements.
